Prioritization Frameworks.hook: Four simple frameworks put your effort on **what truly matters**, not what's loudest
points: Eisenhower Matrix: sort by **urgency and importance** first
Pomodoro: **25 minutes focused**, 5-minute break, longer every 4
Time blocking: keep **deep work and email** apart
80/20: find the **20% driving 80%** of results
Prioritization Frameworks.scene: Your task list is overwhelming on a Monday and **every item feels urgent**. Elias's real priorities are buried somewhere in it.
Prioritization Frameworks.move: Run **the Eisenhower Matrix** first, then block time for the top items
dos: Pick **one framework** for your biggest gap
Step back regularly to **apply the 80/20 rule**
donts: Don't **run all four** from day one
Don't let **the loudest task** set your order

Priority Collision Handling.hook: When two genuine priorities hit at once, **judgment beats speed**
points: A collision: two **important things, neither deferrable**
Weigh the **real cost of delay** on each side
**Partially address both** rather than drop one
Document how it was **resolved and why**
Priority Collision Handling.line: When it's too close to call, **escalate the decision**; never guess
Priority Collision Handling.scene: Within the same minute, Elias needs something urgently and **a major client** needs an answer. Neither can wait.
Priority Collision Handling.move: Weigh what breaks if each waits; **acknowledge one, handle the other**
dos: **Document the resolution** as precedent for next time
Give the waiting side **an interim action**
donts: Don't assume **working faster** solves every collision

Time Management.hook: Decide what deserves time first; **the calendar protects that decision**
points: Time management decides; **calendar management protects**
**Decide** what deserves protected time before touching the calendar
**Block it** before others' requests fill the day
**Review weekly** whether protected time actually held
Time Management.scene: Monday morning, Elias's week is still open. By Tuesday, other people's requests will fill it, and you haven't **decided what deserves protection**.
Time Management.move: Decide first, then **block it today**, before requests arrive
dos: **Review weekly** what held and what slipped
donts: Don't call a block **with no protection** managed
Don't let **whatever feels urgent** always win

Strategic Time Engineering.hook: Treat Elias's time as **capital to invest**, not just spend
points: You're the **portfolio manager** of his time
Align time with **revenue-generating activity**
Protect growth; buffer **compliance and legal deadlines**
Guard reputation-sensitive events and **personal commitments**
Strategic Time Engineering.scene: You review a typical week on Elias's calendar against the five categories. **One category** gets far less protection than the others.
Strategic Time Engineering.move: Name the gap, find why, and **re-engineer the allocation**
donts: Don't protect time **only after a disruption**
Don't call **unscheduled time** a protected block

When Time Management Fails Despite a Cle.hook: A **conflict-free calendar** can still fail the work that matters most
points: Check for **reactive-meeting saturation**, not just conflicts
Confirm **protected space exists** for this week's top work
Travel weeks need discipline **before, during and after**
Diagnose the failure: **the decision or the protection**
When Time Management Fails Despite a Cle.scene: Elias's week looked fine on paper, with no overlaps. Yet **the priority work never got done**, crowded out by reactive meetings.
When Time Management Fails Despite a Cle.move: Diagnose it: wrong priorities, or **right priorities not defended**
dos: Review the pattern **weekly**, not after breakage
Apply the same check to **travel weeks**
donts: Don't equate **no overlaps** with good management
Don't let **reactive meetings** crowd out priorities

Energy Management vs. Time Management.hook: Time asks when; energy asks **can this be done well** right now
points: Most people have **a predictable energy pattern**
Protect the **sharp-focus window** for work that needs it
Flag high-stakes items in **a known low-energy window**
Rhythms shift with role, travel, life: **revisit periodically**
Energy Management vs. Time Management.scene: A high-stakes negotiation is offered a slot in Elias's **known low-energy window**. The slot is open, so it looks fine.
Energy Management vs. Time Management.move: Flag it as **a real risk** before confirming the time
dos: Treat the focus window as **a real scheduling decision**
**Revisit the pattern** after role or travel changes
donts: Don't treat **an open slot as neutral**

Time Management Requires Energy Manageme.hook: An **exhausted executive makes expensive mistakes**, whatever the calendar says
points: Prevent **meeting overload**, even without literal conflicts
Build **recovery buffers** after demanding meetings
Protect deep work; **filter low-leverage requests**
Spot and raise **draining relationships or obligations**
Time Management Requires Energy Manageme.scene: Elias has three back-to-back high-intensity meetings, then a free slot. Someone asks to **book the open slot**.
Time Management Requires Energy Manageme.move: Keep it as **a recovery buffer** and explain why
dos: Raise **draining patterns** instead of silently accommodating
donts: Don't treat **an open slot** as automatically available
Don't fill **every free slot** with meetings

Handling Interruptions Without Losing th.hook: A **two-minute interruption** can cost fifteen minutes of real focus
points: **Triage in seconds**: truly urgent, or just happening now?
**Capture, don't solve**: write it where you'll see it
**Return deliberately** and finish the thought you were on
**Batch the non-urgent** into one later block
Handling Interruptions Without Losing th.scene: You're mid-task when a colleague drops by with a request. It feels urgent because **it's happening right now**.
Handling Interruptions Without Losing th.move: Triage fast, **capture it**, finish your thought, batch it later
dos: Finish **the thought you were on** first
donts: Don't handle captured items **one at a time**

Mid-Stage Task Injections.hook: **Dropped threads** from interrupted work cause some of the most common errors
points: An injection pauses your task; **it rarely cancels it**
Triage: **act now or log it** until a safe stop
**Leave a marker** exactly where you stopped
If fully interrupting, **tell whoever's waiting**
Mid-Stage Task Injections.scene: You're halfway through **a detailed client response** when an urgent, unrelated request lands.
Mid-Stage Task Injections.move: **Mark your place**, triage the new task, then resume deliberately
dos: Keep an **'in progress, paused here'** list

The Two-Minute Rule.hook: If it **truly takes under two minutes**, do it now
points: Tracking a tiny task **costs more than finishing it**
Estimate **honestly, not hopefully**
If it starts expanding, **stop and schedule it**
Stops small tasks becoming **an overwhelming backlog**
The Two-Minute Rule.scene: A quick confirmation email lands that would take a minute. Your list already holds **several items like it**, sitting for days.
The Two-Minute Rule.move: **Send it now**, then clear the qualifying items on the list
dos: Check your list for **lingering two-minute items**
donts: Don't list tasks **quicker done than tracked**

Batch Processing Similar Tasks.hook: Group similar tasks to **cut the cost of switching** between kinds of work
points: All calls in one block, **all replies in another**
Batching **deliberately delays** some tasks slightly
Best for tasks **without a hard deadline**
**Genuinely urgent items** still break the batch
Batch Processing Similar Tasks.scene: Five vendor callbacks arrive across the morning, none with a hard deadline. You've been **returning each as it lands**.
Batch Processing Similar Tasks.move: Hold them for **one call block** later in the day
donts: Don't **hold an urgent item** for the batch

The Cost of Context-Switching.hook: **23 minutes**: the average time to regain full focus after a significant interruption
points: Voluntary switching **costs as much as interruptions**
Batching and focus blocks **cut re-entry costs**
Multitasking different work is **almost always slower**
**Close out one task** before starting the next
The Cost of Context-Switching.scene: You toggle between a spreadsheet, an email draft and a travel booking all morning. It feels productive, but **nothing is finished**.
The Cost of Context-Switching.move: Work them **one at a time**, closing each before switching
dos: Use **focus blocks** to reduce re-entry costs

Dual-Role Context Switching.hook: Switching between **business and personal modes** carries real risk if done carelessly
points: **Name the domain** before responding to any request
**Reset between domains** so tone doesn't bleed across
Keep business and personal **tracking separate**
Switching is **a skill you practice** deliberately
Dual-Role Context Switching.scene: You're mid-draft on **a formal client email** when Sarah Thorne asks about a family event.
Dual-Role Context Switching.move: Close out the client draft, reset, **then answer Sarah warmly**
dos: **Finish one domain** before opening the other
donts: Don't carry **formal tone into personal** messages
Don't **merge business and personal** task tracking

Weekly Planning Rituals.hook: A **short weekly plan** prevents the Monday-morning scramble
points: Review **the week ahead**, not just today
Decide whether **last week's leftovers** still matter
Block time now for **multi-day lead time** items
**Protect the ritual** like any real commitment
Weekly Planning Rituals.scene: A deadline is three days out but **needs prep starting today**. Only a weekly review would catch it in time.
Weekly Planning Rituals.move: **Block prep time now**, not the day it becomes urgent
donts: Don't **bump the session** for something urgent
Don't let **unfinished items** silently roll forward

Saying No Without Damaging Relationships.hook: Yes to everything just **moves the disappointment** to later
points: **Respond promptly**, even when the answer is no
Give **the real, specific reason**
Offer **a genuine alternative** where possible
Be honest up front **about your capacity**
Saying No Without Damaging Relationships.scene: A colleague asks you to take on a project this week. Given your current load, **you can't before Thursday**.
Saying No Without Damaging Relationships.move: Say so now, **give the reason**, offer a later date or partial version
donts: Don't go silent or give **a flat no**

Setting Realistic Deadlines.hook: A deadline set without counting the work is **a guess, not a commitment**
points: **Account for the real work** before naming a date
**Check with whoever does the work** first
Build **real buffer for uncertainty**, not blind padding
Every deadline needs **a clear owner**
Setting Realistic Deadlines.scene: Elias asks when a report will be ready. A colleague is doing the work, and **you haven't asked them yet**.
Setting Realistic Deadlines.move: Check with them, **add honest buffer**, then commit with an owner

Time Tracking Done Right.hook: Accurate time logs show **where time really goes**, billable or not
points: **Log as you work**, not at week's end
Write **specific descriptions** someone can review later
Log small tasks and **communications** too
Build a **Weekly Time Summary**, even for non-billable work
Time Tracking Done Right.scene: It's Friday, and you're rebuilding the week's time entries **from memory**. Calls and quick emails for Elias are missing.
Time Tracking Done Right.move: Log entries **as you work**, starting Monday

The Weekly Time Audit.hook: Your sense of where time goes is usually wrong; **an audit shows the truth**
points: Track **one representative week** of actual activity
Compare against **what you thought mattered**
A periodic check **to catch drift**, not forever
**Act on the findings** in next week's plan
The Weekly Time Audit.scene: You track one representative week and compare it with the priorities you believed you had. **The gap is the finding**.
The Weekly Time Audit.move: **Change next week's plan** based on what the audit revealed

Data Entry That Holds Up.hook: Clean data **before it goes anywhere**, in the same order every time
points: Step 1: **de-duplicate** before anything else
Step 2: **standardize formatting** across every field
Step 3: **validate against source** documents
Step 4: **sort** by the relevant columns
Data Entry That Holds Up.line: Never submit **raw data** for someone downstream to fix
Data Entry That Holds Up.scene: You're about to send Elias a contact list merged from three sources. Some names appear twice and **phone formats don't match**.
Data Entry That Holds Up.move: De-duplicate, standardize, **check against source**, then sort
dos: Follow the four steps **in that order**

Spreadsheet Essentials: Sort, Filter, Lo.hook: A few core spreadsheet skills **turn hours into minutes**
points: **One header row**, one row per record, no merged cells
Five tools: sort, filter, dedupe, **lookups, pivot tables**
**COUNTIF and SUMIF** answer most how-many, how-much questions
**Always sort the whole table**, never one column
Spreadsheet Essentials: Sort, Filter, Lo.scene: Elias wants, by tomorrow, **travel spend per matter** last quarter. You have 400 expense rows with dates, matters, categories and amounts.
Spreadsheet Essentials: Sort, Filter, Lo.move: Make it a table, filter travel, **pivot by matter**
dos: Keep **raw data and summaries** on separate tabs
Enter dates as **real dates**, not text
donts: Don't **sort one column** on its own

Research as a Core EA Skill.hook: Research is **the quiet discipline** under most of the EA role
points: **Vet vendors and contacts** before committing time or money
Brief **who's in the room** and what's at stake
**Fact-check before forwarding** anything as fact
Go to **the primary source** first
Research as a Core EA Skill.line: Never present **unverified information** as settled fact
Research as a Core EA Skill.scene: A new vendor describes itself impressively, and Elias is about to **commit time and money**. You haven't checked their actual standing.
Research as a Core EA Skill.move: **Verify independently** before scheduling, or flag them as unconfirmed
dos: Flag it **unconfirmed** when time runs out
donts: Don't stop at **the first search result**

Research Method & the Real Failure Mode.hook: The real failure isn't laziness; it's **trusting a single source**
points: Start at **the primary source**, then secondary summaries
Cross-check anything **driving a decision or dollar amount**
**Calibrate depth** to the stakes
A vendor's own claims **aren't verification**
Research Method & the Real Failure Mode.scene: A vendor's own site lists impressive credentials, and the fee is significant. That's **one source**, and it's theirs.
Research Method & the Real Failure Mode.move: Find **a second, independent source** before treating it as confirmed
dos: Get **an independent source** for big decisions

Creating and Maintaining a Comprehensive.hook: A contact list is **operational infrastructure**, not a phone book
points: Capture **context, preferred method** and their assistant's name
**Categorize on purpose**: business, personal, vendor, medical, legal
**Update immediately** after any interaction with new info
Test: could **a stand-in find anyone** in seconds?
Creating and Maintaining a Comprehensive.scene: On a call, a contact mentions they now prefer email and you should **always CC his EA**.
Creating and Maintaining a Comprehensive.move: **Update the entry now**, including the standing note
dos: Record **standing notes** like 'always CC his EA'
Build it so **anyone stepping in** can use it
donts: Don't defer updates to **a cleanup session**

Contact List Failure Modes & Upkeep.hook: The biggest risk isn't missing contacts; it's **stale ones**
points: Watch for **old assistants, changed numbers, outdated categories**
**Centralize in one system**, not scattered copies
A **quarterly 10-minute audit** prevents slow rot
**Fix stale entries immediately** when you find them
Contact List Failure Modes & Upkeep.scene: A key vendor's details live on a personal phone, an old spreadsheet and email signatures. **They don't agree**.
Contact List Failure Modes & Upkeep.move: **Consolidate into one system** and fix discrepancies now
dos: Treat three partial lists **as one problem**
donts: Don't split contacts **across phone and spreadsheets**

Master Contact List Discipline.hook: **One master list** the whole team uses, because copies drift invisibly
points: **Personal copies** drift out of sync
Know **who to loop in** for each meeting type
**Update the master** the moment a change is known
A discrepancy means **reinforce single-source discipline**
Master Contact List Discipline.scene: Two assistants keep their own copies of a key contact. In a time-sensitive moment, the call goes to **a disconnected number**.
Master Contact List Discipline.move: Retire personal copies; keep **one master list** current

Client Relationship Management.hook: CRM is how relationships **grow after the first yes**
points: **Log every interaction** so the next touch starts accurate
Be **proactive**: renewals, promised follow-ups, relevant updates
Segment by **relationship stage**
**Check history** before any client call or email
Client Relationship Management.scene: A client closed three months ago was never contacted again. Now they email a question **hinting at a competitor**.
Client Relationship Management.move: Answer promptly, reference their history, and **rebuild the relationship**
donts: Don't let the CRM become **where data dies**
Don't let **a promised follow-up** go unlogged

CRM Software Fundamentals.hook: A CRM is only as good as **what you put in it**
points: Three core objects: **contacts, deals, activities**
The CRM is **the single source of truth** for status
**Map pipeline stages** to your real process first
Use custom fields and **built-in reminders**, not side lists
CRM Software Fundamentals.scene: You inherit 40 open deals, most untouched for months. Elias wants **an accurate pipeline forecast** by end of day.
CRM Software Fundamentals.move: Close or reactivate stale deals, **reset honest stages**, then forecast
donts: Don't **create a contact** without searching first
Don't bury trackable data **in notes fields**

Data Hygiene & Deduplication.hook: Duplicates and stale records **fragment a contact's history**
points: **Data decays on its own** every month
Search by **name, company and email domain** before adding
**Merge forward**, keeping both records' history
**Clean bounces and unsubscribes** on a schedule
Data Hygiene & Deduplication.scene: You find **three records** for what seems to be the same person at the same company, each with different interaction history.
Data Hygiene & Deduplication.move: Verify it's one person, then **merge forward** with all history
donts: Don't merge by **deleting the thinner record**

Sales Mindset.hook: Sales is **solving a real problem** for the other person, not persuading
points: Know **what problem they have** before any outreach
Bring **real curiosity**, not a script
Rejection is **information, not failure**
**Track outcomes honestly**, rejections included
Sales Mindset.scene: You've sent 15 cold outreach emails this week and received **zero responses**.
Sales Mindset.move: Treat it as information: **review targeting and message**, keep going
dos: **Invest more** in leads that deserve it
Use the same skill **for internal buy-in**

Cold Calling, Appointment Setting & Lead.hook: A cold call's goal is **a warmer second conversation**, rarely the close
points: **Research before calling**: specifics beat scripts
Open with **a brief, relevant value proposition**
Guard outbound contact lists **like confidential email**
**Log every call outcome** immediately
Cold Calling, Appointment Setting & Lead.scene: Before calling a prospect on Elias's behalf, you find **a current, specific reference** about their business.
Cold Calling, Appointment Setting & Lead.move: **Open with that reference** and a brief value proposition, not a pitch
donts: Don't treat contact lists **with less discretion**

How to Generate Leads for Business.hook: Lead generation **finds the lead**; cold calling works it
points: Draw from **more than one channel**
Qualify on **fit, need, authority, timeline**
First contact: **researched, specific, brief**
**A lead not logged** is a lead lost
How to Generate Leads for Business.scene: A promising contact surfaces through **a past client's referral**. Nobody has logged it yet.
How to Generate Leads for Business.move: **Qualify it, log it**, then make a researched first contact

Lead Generation & Data Sourcing.hook: **Data quality** decides whether every outreach effort downstream pays off
points: Confirm **role, company context and recent activity** first
Verify contacts at **the primary source**
Capture **qualifying details** at the point of sourcing
A few **well-sourced leads** beat a long loose list
Lead Generation & Data Sourcing.scene: You need **50 leads by end of day** for a campaign. Verifying each one properly will take real time.
Lead Generation & Data Sourcing.move: Hit what you can verify; **don't trade accuracy for volume**
dos: **Refresh lead lists** before they go stale

Manual Lead Generation Methods.hook: Manual methods are slow but produce **the leads most likely to convert**
points: Start with **referrals** from clients and partners
**Log event contacts** in the CRM the same day
**Record the source** of every lead
Bar rules apply: **the attorney approves every approach**
Manual Lead Generation Methods.line: Never approach someone **needing help with a specific matter**; take it to the attorney
Manual Lead Generation Methods.scene: Thorne & Partners is launching a Data Privacy & Cybersecurity practice. Elias wants **20 companies to approach by Friday**, manual methods only.
Manual Lead Generation Methods.move: Start with referrals and registries; **get Elias's approval** before approaching
dos: **Ten fitting leads** beat a hundred copied names
List **people worth meeting** before an event
donts: Don't log business cards **a week later**
Don't contact someone just because **their name is public**

Automated Lead Generation Tools & Workfl.hook: Automation saves hours, but **a person verifies every lead**
points: Forms, alerts and enrichment **feed one place: the CRM**
Set **duplicate checks** on email and company
Each new lead creates **a task to verify within a day**
**Name one owner** for every automation
Automated Lead Generation Tools & Workfl.line: **Nothing goes to a prospect** until a person approves it
Automated Lead Generation Tools & Workfl.scene: The webinar form creates 40 CRM records a week, and partners complain that **most are students and vendors**.
Automated Lead Generation Tools & Workfl.move: Keep the form; route new leads to **a verification task first**
donts: Don't load **a bought list** into sequences

Verifying a Working Lead.hook: A few minutes of verification separates **a real lead** from a name
points: Confirm **the person still holds the role**
Confirm the business is **active and fits**
Check **email domain and phone** actually reach them
**Clear it**: duplicates, do-not-contact list, conflict check
Verifying a Working Lead.line: Never approach **an existing client's opponent**; run the conflict check
Verifying a Working Lead.scene: Your list shows Dana Reyes at Brightline Logistics. **Dana left in March**, the email domain is misspelled, and **Brightline merged**.
Verifying a Working Lead.move: Mark it **Not workable**, with reason, date and who checked
donts: Don't treat **a bounce as bad luck**

Lead Quality, Qualifying & Tracking.hook: **Referrals** arrive with trust a cold list never has
points: **Ask satisfied clients** for referrals; don't wait
**Qualify early**: fit, need, authority, timeline
**Log every lead** the moment it exists
The difference is **follow-through**, not first touch
Lead Quality, Qualifying & Tracking.scene: A promising contact replied warmly to a first email weeks ago. **No one followed up**, and the lead has gone cold.
Lead Quality, Qualifying & Tracking.move: **Log it, follow up now**, and track every next step
dos: Feed qualified leads into **the contact list**

Appointment Setting (BANT/MEDDPICC).hook: **Qualify before you schedule**: a meeting must be worth both sides' time
points: **BANT**: budget, authority, need, timeline, as a quick check
**MEDDPICC** for complex, high-value, multi-stakeholder deals
Let qualified leads **pick a slot** via Calendly or Bookings
**Remind 24-48 hours prior** with agenda and prep
Appointment Setting (BANT/MEDDPICC).scene: A prospect enthusiastically wants a call right now, but you haven't confirmed **budget or decision authority**.
Appointment Setting (BANT/MEDDPICC).move: Ask **a few qualifying questions** before booking, keeping their interest
dos: **Confirm and remind** close to the meeting
donts: Don't book just because of **a fast yes**

Cold Outbound Execution.hook: Outbound is where research **pays off or doesn't**
points: Open with **something specific** to the recipient
Keep the ask **small: 15 minutes**
**Prepare for likely objections**, not just the opener
**Listen more than you talk** once it starts
Cold Outbound Execution.scene: On a cold call, the prospect says **'I'm not interested'** right after your opening line.
Cold Outbound Execution.move: Ask **one clarifying question**, or offer to follow up gracefully
dos: Use the script **as a starting point**

Handling Sales Objections Beyond the Scr.hook: Diagnose **what the objection really means** before you answer it
points: Most objections: **information, trust or timing**
Ask **one clarifying question** first
**Acknowledge specifically** before addressing it
Timing issue? **Get a specific follow-up date**
Handling Sales Objections Beyond the Scr.line: Never **push past a real no**; it closes future doors
Handling Sales Objections Beyond the Scr.scene: A prospect says **'we already have a vendor for this'**. Happy, locked in, or just politely ending the call?
Handling Sales Objections Beyond the Scr.move: Ask **one clarifying question** to learn which, then adapt
dos: Accept when it's **genuinely not the right fit**

Pipeline Reporting & Forecasting Basics.hook: A forecast is only as honest as **the deal stages under it**
points: Apply **realistic, historical probabilities** per stage
Separate **committed from best case**
**Flag deals stuck** in a stage too long
Review **weekly, same day, same format**
Pipeline Reporting & Forecasting Basics.scene: Elias asks for a realistic quarterly forecast. Two **early-stage deals** make up **60% of the raw total**.
Pipeline Reporting & Forecasting Basics.move: Report the weighted number and **flag both deals' risk** explicitly

Email Marketing vs. Cold Outreach.hook: **Marketing and cold outreach** follow different rules; mixing them hurts the firm
points: Marketing: **one message to many** who know the firm
Outreach: **one-to-one**, individually relevant, low-volume
**Keep the lists separate**, recording how each joined
**Attorney approves** every template and script
Email Marketing vs. Cold Outreach.line: Never send **bulk marketing** from the attorney's personal mailbox
Email Marketing vs. Cold Outreach.scene: Elias hands you **400 business cards** from a legal-tech conference and asks you to send everyone the newsletter.
Email Marketing vs. Cold Outreach.move: Don't add them silently; **offer opt-in or one-to-one outreach**

Outreach Compliance Basics.hook: Outreach is regulated; **violations carry real legal and financial risk**
points: **CAN-SPAM** for email; do-not-call and TCPA for phone, text
**Each channel** has its own rules
**Honor opt-outs** immediately and completely
**Record consent** or relationship basis for every list
Outreach Compliance Basics.line: Confirm **the firm's policy or counsel**, not general knowledge
Outreach Compliance Basics.scene: A colleague hands you a conference contact list for a new campaign, with **no notes on how it was collected**.
Outreach Compliance Basics.move: **Confirm provenance and consent** before sending anything
dos: Include **a working opt-out** on every email

Building & Segmenting an Email List.hook: A small list **who want to hear from you** beats a big one
points: Record **source and consent** for every contact
**Tag on entry**: source, date, interest, relationship
Start with **Clients, Referral Partners, Prospects**
**Clean quarterly**: bounces, duplicates, unsubscribes, 12-month non-openers
Building & Segmenting an Email List.line: Keep **opposing parties and conflicts** off every marketing list
Building & Segmenting an Email List.scene: A partner wants the estate-planning newsletter sent **'to everyone'**: 1,800 contacts, including **opposing counsel** from past matters.
Building & Segmenting an Email List.move: **Segment by relationship**, excluding opposing counsel and conflicts
dos: Add **practice-area segments** as the list grows

Writing Outreach Emails That Get Replies.hook: Short, specific, **one easy ask**: that's what gets replies
points: Keep it to **50–125 words**
Open with **why them, specifically**
Subject lines: **clear and honest**, never misleading
One ask: **'a 15-minute call next week?'**
Writing Outreach Emails That Get Replies.line: Never state or imply **a guaranteed legal outcome**
Writing Outreach Emails That Get Replies.scene: A draft to a founder whose startup just raised a Series A opens with **the firm's history**.
Writing Outreach Emails That Get Replies.move: Open with **their Series A**, then one line of value
donts: Don't lead with **firm history and awards**

Email Outreach Sequencing & Follow-Up Ca.hook: Most replies come from **the follow-ups**, not the first touch
points: Space follow-ups **3-5 business days** apart
**Add a new angle** at every step
End with **a clear close-the-loop** message
Track **reply rate by step**
Email Outreach Sequencing & Follow-Up Ca.scene: A prospect **opened your first three emails** but never replied. One email remains in your sequence.
Email Outreach Sequencing & Follow-Up Ca.move: Send **a courteous close-out** that leaves the door open

Email Deliverability Basics.hook: A damaged domain can push **even client emails into spam**
points: **SPF, DKIM and DMARC** authenticate the firm's email
**One-click unsubscribe** in every marketing email
Keep **hard bounces under about 2%**, complaints under 0.3%
**Warm up** new domains and platforms gradually
Email Deliverability Basics.scene: After the last newsletter, three clients say **firm emails are landing in spam**.
Email Deliverability Basics.move: **Involve IT**: check SPF, DKIM, DMARC and the send report
dos: Use **a marketing subdomain** for bulk mail

Email Metrics & A/B Testing.hook: Judge emails by **replies and consultations**, not opens alone
points: **Open rates** are inflated by Apple Mail Privacy Protection
**Pick the goal metric** before sending
A/B tests **change one thing only**
Compare to **the firm's own averages**
Email Metrics & A/B Testing.scene: Subject A: **42% opens, 1 reply**. Subject B: 31% opens, **6 replies**.
Email Metrics & A/B Testing.move: **Subject B won**; tell the attorney replies matter more
donts: Don't call **a winner from tiny numbers**

Law Firm Email Newsletters.hook: A newsletter keeps the firm **top-of-mind** between matters
points: **Consistency beats frequency**: monthly or quarterly, reliably
Lead with **information the reader can use**
Every issue gets **attorney review and sign-off**
**Archive every issue** with its approval date
Law Firm Email Newsletters.line: Never name **a client, matter or outcome** without documented consent
Law Firm Email Newsletters.scene: Elias wants this month's newsletter to celebrate **a big settlement win**, with the client's company in the headline.
Law Firm Email Newsletters.move: Get **documented client consent** first; without it, drop the name
dos: Add **a disclaimer** where the jurisdiction requires
**Send a test** to yourself and a reviewer
donts: Don't make it **only about the firm**

Email Marketing Tools & Approval Workflo.hook: A written approval workflow **protects the firm** from one bad send
points: Draft → review → **compliance check** → schedule → report
Templates carry **firm address, unsubscribe and disclaimer**
**Limit send permission** in the platform
**Save every sent version** and approval note
Email Marketing Tools & Approval Workflo.line: No **'quick send' skips review**, even under time pressure
Email Marketing Tools & Approval Workflo.scene: Elias wants an event invitation sent tonight, but **the reviewing associate** is unavailable until tomorrow.
Email Marketing Tools & Approval Workflo.move: Don't skip review: **ask Elias to review it**, or send tomorrow

Email Outreach End-to-End: Research, Wri.hook: An outreach email is judged in **about three seconds** on a phone
points: **One verified, specific fact** beats clever phrasing
Every email has **exactly one job**: a small yes
**Plan the sequence** before the first send
**Stop the moment** they reply or opt out
Email Outreach End-to-End: Research, Wri.line: Only the attorney speaks to a matter; **never promise outcomes**
Email Outreach End-to-End: Research, Wri.scene: A regional construction company just announced **a two-state expansion**. Your first email to its operations director got **no reply after four days**.
Email Outreach End-to-End: Research, Wri.move: Follow up with **a new angle**; close out around day 8–10
dos: **Read it on a phone** before sending
donts: Don't swap **only the name** in templates
